params.body:
## What the editor ran into

Writing a post in the Write view, a heading typed as `## Why It Matters` with its paragraph on the next line (no blank line between them) showed as one large bold heading holding the whole paragraph. Clicking it brought back the raw markdown, clicking elsewhere turned the next one into a heading. It was impossible to tell what gentells.com would show.

Every post is also written in the same sections, and each new post started from an empty sheet, so they were typed by hand every time.

## What changes

**Headings end at their line.** gentells.com renders the body as CommonMark (`Str::markdown`), and the pipeline's projection passes the body through unchanged: a heading line, then a paragraph, also when a heading line stands in the middle of a paragraph. `blockOf` in Writing.jsx made the whole paragraph the heading. Now `blocksOf` (piece.js) cuts a paragraph into blocks where CommonMark does, with every line's offset kept so source numbers land where they did. When the writer leaves a paragraph that has a heading line inside it, it is split into the heading and its text (`headingsApart`), so the stored paragraphs are the ones the site shows and the pipeline counts. Checked against the site's own CommonMark converter on the same text.

**A new post opens laid out in its sections.** Signal, Why It Matters, Examples, How To Activate It with `### Monday:` and `### This quarter:` under it, taken from the 78 posts live on gentells.com (levels and spelling as there; the two subheadings carry a title after the colon). The Opportunity keeps its own fields under the body.

- The sections are laid out by the editor over an empty body (`postLayout`), in quiet grey with "Write here" under each. Clicking writes under a section; clicking a heading edits it (Monday: gets its title).
- A section is stored only once something is written under it. A section still exactly as laid out, with nothing under it, is left out on save (`withoutEmptySections`), so an untouched post stays empty for `pieceStage`, the empty-piece opening, autosave, the desk's blank-piece reuse and the claim check, and no empty heading reaches gentells.com. A heading the writer typed or changed is kept even when empty (two live posts have a subheading broken over two lines by the PDF import; they are left alone).
- Missing sections are shown in their place around what is written, so a draft written over several sittings keeps its shape. Sections are laid out only over a post with nothing written yet (a picture or a heading at most) or one that already uses them; a post written another way, articles and decks keep what they have. Any heading with nothing under it gets a "Write here".
- Headings no longer count as writing in `pieceStage`. Reading along reads a heading glued to its text for that text.

**Where the template lives.** `POST_SECTIONS` in `src/piece.js`, one list. The Studio is the only place that lays a post out, and nothing about the template is stored or sent: the pipeline and the site see a body like any other. A later change of structure is one edit there.

## Checked

- `npm test`: 62/62, new tests for blocks, heading split, layout, empty sections and pieceStage.
- `vite build` clean.
- Local Studio against a local pipeline on a copy of the production database: the glued heading before and after, a new post laid out, writing under two sections stores only those (with How To Activate It brought along under This quarter:), an untouched new post stores an empty body.

Not changed: the writing partner's prompt still describes a post generically, so a first draft written by the conversation does not use these sections yet.

Safe to merge alone; no pipeline or site change needed.
params.title: Headings end at their line in the editor; a new post opens laid out in its sections
